findings: Owner request 2026-11-09: practice long questions for Chapter 3 in the same format as the Physics chapter practice, long questions in the Computer Science Board shape (8 marks each) (English and Roman Urdu), written from the chapter; not printed in the book. 15 questions numbered 1-15; by section: 3.1.1.1 1, 3.2.1.3 1, 3.3.2 1, 3.3.3.2 1, 3.4.1.1 2, 3.4.1~2 1, 3.5.1 1, 3.6.1 1, 3.6.1~2 1, 3.6.1~3 1, 3.6.1.1 1, 3.6.2.1 1, 3.7.2.2 1, 3.7.3.2 1.

Covers computational problems and their classes, algorithms and linear search, Generate and Test, solvability and intractability, Class P and NP, Big O and a growth-rate table, space complexity, efficiency, scalability and suitability, Merge Sort, greedy Coin Change, Dynamic Programming for Fibonacci, Selection Sort, Binary Search and BFS/DFS traces. Every trace and number was computed in Python. The exercise's long questions (all four complexity classes, Halting Problem, linear vs binary search, optimization problems, N-Queens backtracking, Bubble Sort process, time vs space complexity) are not repeated. Book corrections followed: n(n − 1)/2 pair comparisons, binary search target 7, Cons not Cones.
Every question carries a book_ref (topic id and exact words of that topic's English lesson), verified by tools.py.
The Roman Urdu file has the same checkpoints, order and book_refs; each prompt keeps the English question with the Roman Urdu meaning in brackets.
Drafts for the academic review (second-person review before publication).
